newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly down in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly down in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down in slow trading on Tuesday due to overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 20,130 yuan ($2,424) per tonne, down 10 yuan. It opened at 20,100 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 20,160 and a low of 20,080.
October rose 20 to 20,700 yuan. November was unchanged at 20,450. December fell 30 to 20,170, February 10 to 20,140 and March 30 to 20,170.
Combined volume fell to 19,510 tonnes from 27,340.
Copper opened down and moved in a very narrow range of 50 yuan for most of the session.
Traders said most investors stayed on the sidelines on unclear short-term direction and lack of market-moving news.
"The LME did not give a clear direction and many investors took a wait-and-watch attitude," one trader said.
"Copper is likely to move between 20,000 and 20,500 until market-moving news emerges," he added.
Traders said copper would not fall sharply despite poor fundamentals and that institutional support and short-covering by individuals would support copper at 20,000 yuan.
Aluminium ended down. October fell 120 to 13,930 yuan and November 250 to 13,800.
Combined volume rose to 870 tonnes from 300.
